transcript.en: Ah …come in, Russ.
transcript.zh: 啊，进来，罗斯。

transcript.en: Thank you.
transcript.zh: 谢谢。

transcript.en: Now you wanted to consult me about your class presentation on nanotechnology
transcript.zh: 你现在是想问问我关于纳米技术的课堂演示，

transcript.en: you're due to give it in next week, aren't you?
transcript.zh: 你下周就要做了是吧？

transcript.en: That's right. And I’m really struggling.
transcript.zh: 是的，我现在很纠结。

transcript.en: I chose the topic because I didn't know much about it and wanted to learn more,
transcript.zh: 我选择这个话题是对它了解不多，

transcript.en: but now I've read so much about it, in a way there's too much to say -I could talk for much longer than the twenty minutes I've been allocated.
transcript.zh: 但是我想了解更多，现在我读了很多关于这方面的书，在某种程度上可以说太多了，我讲的时间远远可以超过给我分配的20分钟。

transcript.en: Should I assume the other students don't know much, and give them a kind of general introduction,
transcript.zh: 我是应该假设其他学生知道的不多，然后给他们做一个大概的介绍呢，

transcript.en: or should I try and make them share my fascination with a particular aspect?
transcript.zh: 还是从一个方面入手，让他们了解我对纳米技术的迷恋之处。

transcript.en: You could do either, but you'll need to have it clear in your own mind.
transcript.zh: 哪种都可以，但是你得构思清楚。

transcript.en: Then I think I'll give an overview.
transcript.zh: 然后我想做一下概述。

transcript.en: OK. Now, one way of approaching this is to work through developments in chronological order.
transcript.zh: 好的，其中一条采取方式就是以时间顺序来展开描述。

transcript.en: Uh-huh.
transcript.zh: 嗯嗯。

transcript.en: On the other hand, you could talk about the numerous ways that nanotechnology is being applied.
transcript.zh: 另一方面，你可以讨论一下纳米技术的许多应用。

transcript.en: You mean things like thin films on camera displays to make them water-repellent, and additives to make motorcycle helmets stronger and lighter.
transcript.zh: 你是指像相机显示屏上用于防水的薄膜，以及能让摩托车头盔更坚固、更轻便的添加剂这类东西吗？

transcript.en: Exactly. Or another way would be to focus on its impact in one particular area, say medicine, or space exploration.
transcript.zh: 是的，另一方面可以专门关注纳米技术对某一方面的影响，例如医药或太空探索。

transcript.en: That would make it easier to focus.
transcript.zh: 这样会使议题更加容易进行。

transcript.en: Perhaps I should do that.
transcript.zh: 也许我应该得这么做。

transcript.en: I think that would be a good idea.
transcript.zh: 我认为那是个好主意。

transcript.en: Right How important is it to include slides in the presentation?
transcript.zh: 好的，在课堂展示中包含幻灯片有多重要？

transcript.en: They aren't essential, by any means.
transcript.zh: 总而言之，它们都不是必需的。

transcript.en: And there's a danger of tailoring what you say to fit whatever slides you can find.
transcript.zh: 还有一个你需要注意的地方，就是你所找的幻灯片得符合你所讲的主题。

transcript.en: While it can be good to include slides, you could end up spending too Iong looking for suitable ones.
transcript.zh: 加入幻灯片是好事，但是寻找合适的幻灯片会花很长时间。

transcript.en: You might find it better to leave them out.
transcript.zh: 我觉得你最好还是不要加入幻灯片。

transcript.en: I see. Another thing I was wondering about was how to start.
transcript.zh: 我明白了，另一件我想知道的事情是如何开始。

transcript.en: I know presentations often begin with ‘ First I'm going to talk about this, and then I'll talk about that ’,
transcript.zh: 我知道课堂展示通常是以“首先我要讲的是，然后接下来是”为开头，

transcript.en: but I thought about asking the audience what they know about nanotechnology.
transcript.zh: 但是我想问观众他们对纳米技术了解有多少。

transcript.en: That would be fine if you had an hour or two for the presentation,
transcript.zh: 如果你有一两个小时，那还可以。

transcript.en: but you might find that you can't do anything with the answers you get, and it simply eats into the short time that's available.
transcript.zh: 但是最终也许你会意识到你对获得的答案也不能做什么改变，而它们也只是会占用你有效的时间。

transcript.en: So, maybe I should mention a particular way that nanotechnology is used, to focus people's attention.
transcript.zh: 那么，也许我应该讲讲纳米技术的某一特殊运用，以引起人们的注意。

transcript.en: That sounds sensible.
transcript.zh: 嗯，这听起来还蛮有道理的。

transcript.en: What do you think I should do next ? I really have to plan the presentation today and tomorrow.
transcript.zh: 你觉得我下一步该做什么，我今明两天真的要准备课堂展示的事情了。

transcript.en: Well, initially I think you should ignore all the notes you've made, take a small piece of paper,
transcript.zh: 首先，我认为你应该忽略掉你所作的所有笔记，备一张小纸条，

transcript.en: and write a single short sentence that ties together the whole presentation:
transcript.zh: 然后在上面写下串起整篇展示的简短句子。

transcript.en: it can be something as simple as ‘ Nanotechnology is already improving our lives ’.
transcript.zh: 可以就用这么简单的句子，例如“纳米技术已经改善了我们的生活”。

transcript.en: Then start planning the content around that.
transcript.zh: 然后围绕句子开始做内容展开。

transcript.en: You can always modify that sentence later, if you need to.
transcript.zh: 你可以稍后再修改一下句子，如果有需要的话。

transcript.en: OK.
transcript.zh: 好的。

transcript.en: OK, now let's think about actually giving the presentation.
transcript.zh: 好的，那现在让我们思考一下如何开展演讲。

transcript.en: You've only given one before, if I remember correctly, about an experiment you'd been involved in.
transcript.zh: 如果我没记错的话，你之前就做过一个课堂展示，内容是你参与的一次实验。

transcript.en: That's right. It was pretty rubbish!
transcript.zh: 是的，不过那次我讲得太差了。

transcript.en: Let's say it was better in some respects than in others.
transcript.zh: 我们只能说实验有不足之处，也有可取之处。

transcript.en: With regard to the structure. I felt that you ended rather abruptly, without rounding it off.
transcript.zh: 至于结构，我觉得你结尾时太草率了，没有圆满结束。

transcript.en: Be careful not to do that in next week's presentation.
transcript.zh: 记得不要在下周的课堂展示中重蹈覆辙。

transcript.en: OK.
transcript.zh: 好的。

transcript.en: And you made very little eye contact with the audience, because you were looking down at your notes most of the time.
transcript.zh: 还有你和观众几乎没有眼神交流，因为大多数时间你都低头看着你的笔记。

transcript.en: You need to be looking at the audience and only occasionally glancing at your notes.
transcript.zh: 你需要看一下你的观众然后不时浏览你的笔记。

transcript.en: Mmm.
transcript.zh: 嗯嗯。

transcript.en: Your body language was a little odd.
transcript.zh: 还有你的肢体语言有点奇怪。

transcript.en: Every time you showed a slide, you turned your back on the audience so you could look at it
transcript.zh: 每当你显示一张幻灯片的时候，你都背对着观众，所以你就可以看幻灯片，

transcript.en: you should have been looking at your laptop.
transcript.zh: 你应该要看你的笔记本电脑才是。

transcript.en: And you kept scratching your head, so I found myself wondering when you were next going to do that,
transcript.zh: 还有你一直挠头，所以我就不禁好奇下次你什么时候还要再做那动作，

transcript.en: instead of listening to what you were saying!
transcript.zh: 就不会把注意力放在你要讲的内容上面。

transcript.en: Oh dear. What did you think of the language?
transcript.zh: 天啊。你觉得这语言如何？。

transcript.en: I knew that not everyone was familiar with the subject, so I tried to make it as simple as I could.
transcript.zh: 我知道不是每个人都熟悉这个话题，所以我尽量使内容看起来简单些

transcript.en: Yes, that came across. You used a few words that are specific to the field,
transcript.zh: 嗯，这行得通，你用了几个相关术语，

transcript.en: but you always explained what they meant,
transcript.zh: 但是你一般都解释过它们的意思，

transcript.en: so the audience wouldn’t have had any difficulty understanding.
transcript.zh: 这样子观众就比较容易理解。

transcript.en: Uh-huh.
transcript.zh: 嗯嗯。

transcript.en: I must say the handouts you prepared were well thought out.
transcript.zh: 你准备的讲义框架清晰。

transcript.en: They were a good summary of your presentation, which people would be able to refer to later on.
transcript.zh: 很好地总结了演讲的内容，以后大家可以拿来做参考。

transcript.en: So well done on that.
transcript.zh: 所以你在这方面做得很好。

transcript.en: Thank you.
transcript.zh: 谢谢。

transcript.en: Well, I hope that helps you with next week's presentation.
transcript.zh: 好的，我希望这会对你下周的课堂展示有所帮助。

transcript.en: Yes, it will. Thanks a lot.
transcript.zh: 会的，不胜感激。

transcript.en: I'll look forward to seeing a big improvement, then.
transcript.zh: 那我就期待看到大幅的进步了。
